description: Infrastructure patterns for real-time and batch data ingestion, feature stores, model serving, backtesting frameworks, and MLOps for quantitative finance.

techniques.name: Feature Store Architecture (Feast/Hopsworks/Tecton)
techniques.description: Centralized feature management for ML pipelines. Feast (Linux Foundation, open-source) provides modular online/offline retrieval with BigQuery/Redis backends. Hopsworks offers enterprise-grade governance with RonDB sub-millisecond latency. Tecton is a managed feature platform. All support point-in-time correctness preventing look-ahead bias.
techniques.verification_notes: Feast and Hopsworks verified via official docs. Sub-millisecond Hopsworks RonDB latency confirmed. Point-in-time correctness is a standard feature.

techniques.name: MLOps Pipeline Orchestration
techniques.description: Workflow orchestration for ML model lifecycle: training, validation, deployment, monitoring. Core tools include Airflow (batch), Prefect (event-driven), and Dagster (asset-based). Financial institutions progressing through Level 0-4 maturity model.
techniques.verification_notes: MLOps maturity model confirmed. Market valued at $1.58B in 2024 with 35.5% CAGR verified via multiple market research firms.

techniques.name: Data Versioning & Lineage Tracking
techniques.description: Version control for datasets ensuring reproducibility and regulatory compliance. DVC (Data Version Control) and LakeFS provide git-like versioning for data. Essential for audit trails and experiment reproducibility.
techniques.verification_notes: DVC and LakeFS are well-established tools. Regulatory requirement for data lineage confirmed by SR 11-7 and EU AI Act.

techniques.name: Experiment Tracking & Model Registry
techniques.description: Tracking ML experiments (hyperparameters, metrics, artifacts) and managing model versions through production lifecycle. MLflow is the dominant open-source tool; Weights & Biases offers managed alternative.
techniques.verification_notes: MLflow and W&B widely adopted. Model registry patterns well-documented.

techniques.name: Data Quality & Drift Monitoring
techniques.description: Automated validation of data quality and detection of distribution shifts. Great Expectations provides schema and statistical validation. Evidently AI and WhyLabs monitor production data and model drift.
techniques.verification_notes: Tools verified. Data drift monitoring is critical for financial ML where market regimes shift.

techniques.name: Backtesting Frameworks
techniques.description: Systematic backtesting infrastructure for evaluating trading strategies. VectorBT PRO integrates with portfolio optimization libraries. Backtrader and Zipline provide event-driven backtesting.
techniques.verification_notes: All three frameworks verified. VectorBT PRO integration with PyPortfolioOpt and Riskfolio-Lib confirmed.
